name: Slow-Cooker Chicken Wild Rice Soup
description: A creamy Minnesota classic that cooks itself. Everything goes in the slow cooker early afternoon, and a cream-and-cornstarch stir-in at the end thickens it — no stovetop, no roux, very few dishes.
time: 20 minutes hands-on, 4 hours on high (or 7 on low)
ingredients: 1 cup uncooked wild rice (or wild rice blend), rinsed
instructions: Add the wild rice, carrots, celery, onion, mushrooms, garlic, thyme, salt, pepper, and bay leaf to the slow cooker. Lay the chicken on top and pour in the broth.
Cover and cook on high 4 hours (or low 7) until the rice is tender and split open.
Pull out the chicken and shred it with two forks. Discard the bay leaf.
Whisk the cornstarch into the cream until smooth. Stir it into the soup along with the butter and the shredded chicken.
Cover and cook 15–20 more minutes until thickened. Taste for salt and serve with bread.
tips: Rinse the rice and wash/chop the vegetables before any time the water will be off — after that, there's nothing that needs the sink.
If it gets too thick on standing, loosen with a splash of broth.
Cool a portion for the kids before serving; the rice and soft veggies are easy toddler food.
Keeps 4 days in the fridge; the rice keeps absorbing liquid, so add broth when reheating.
